purpose: The machine-readable rules every KIT consumer follows, whatever its framework. Agents styling any project against KIT read this file before writing interface code.

tokenLaw.rule: Token values are literal and never re-derived, approximated, or renamed. A color, size, or duration must be byte-identical to the published token.
tokenLaw.universalVariables: Pieces intended to work under every complete system may reference only variables present in every complete system's tokens.css.
tokenLaw.neverInvent: Never invent a color, shadow, radius, or duration when a token exists for the role. If no token fits, raise it to the kit instead of hardcoding.

systems.note: Complete systems style the full catalog. Foundation kits supplement a system without replacing its identity.

minimums.controlHeightNote: Effective touch target. A small visual mark (20px checkbox) is allowed inside a row whose hit area is at least 44px.
minimums.focus: Every interactive element shows a visible :focus-visible outline using the ring token.
minimums.keyboard: Every action reachable by pointer is reachable by keyboard.
minimums.contrast: Body text meets readable contrast on its surface in both appearances the system owns.

banned: glow or shadow blooms outside an isolated Signature Effect frame
looping resting motion in product UI

motion.durations: Use the kit-fast and kit-standard duration tokens with the kit-ease curve; motion is short and property-specific.
motion.reducedMotion: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce must make every time-based signal static.
motion.audio: Any sound starts muted behind an explicit control.

language.rule: Product copy is plain English. No jargon, no file formats, no internal system names in primary surfaces.
language.errors: Error messages say what happened, what is safe, and the one next action.
language.emptyStates: Empty screens say what will appear and offer one clear next step.

reversibility.rule: Nothing is un-editable. Destructive actions offer undo or a real rollback path, and a kit swap must keep one reversible appearance switch plus a clean restore.
reversibility.swaps: Product screens, routes, data, and behavior stay owned by the product during a visual-system swap.

proof: Before claiming done: exercise changed controls with pointer and keyboard, check the proof widths for overflow, check both appearances when the system owns both, and check the console is clean.
